audits.title: Using criteria-based audit to improve the management of postpartum haemorrhage in resource limited countries: a case study of Malawi.
audits.standard: Standards for PPH management based on WHO manuals
audits.setting: Maternity units in eight hospitals in Malawi

cycle1.result: Typing and cross-match 65.0%; haematocrit or haemoglobin established 67.5%; fluid intake/output chart 0.0%.

audits.intervention: Audit results presented to providers, who made and implemented recommendations.

cycle2.result: Typing and cross-match 84.4% (P = 0.034); haematocrit or haemoglobin 86.7% (P = 0.029); fluid chart 33.3%.

audits.other_findings: Authors suggest larger samples are needed to assess effect on mortality.
audits.citation: Kongnyuy EJ, Mlava G, van den Broek N. Using criteria-based audit to improve the management of postpartum haemorrhage in resource limited countries: a case study of Malawi. Matern Child Health J. 2009;13(6):873-878. doi:10.1007/s10995-008-0408-3. PMID: 18780170.

audits.title: [Impact of a new regional management for postpartum hemorrhages by an audit of severe cases: a before and after study (2002-2005)].
audits.setting: All birthplaces in Basse-Normandie region; blinded paired obstetrician-anaesthetist review of severe PPH cases

cycle1.result: Inadequate management in 32% of severe PPH cases.

audits.intervention: Regional guidelines for PPH management diffused to all birthplaces in 2004.
audits.other_findings: Quality of care improved across the region but authors note room for further progress.

audits.title: Clinical audit: a useful tool for reducing severe postpartum haemorrhages?
audits.standard: Explicit criteria for recommended procedures in severe postpartum haemorrhage
audits.setting: Two maternity units (level III and level II), Rhône-Alpes

cycle1.result: Severe PPH prevalence 1.52% of deliveries (level III) and 2.08% (level II).

audits.intervention: Quarterly criteria-based clinical audit meetings reviewing all severe PPH cases with feedback to all staff.
audits.citation: Dupont C, Deneux-Tharaux C, Touzet S, Colin C, Bouvier-Colle MH, Lansac J, et al.. Clinical audit: a useful tool for reducing severe postpartum haemorrhages?. Int J Qual Health Care. 2011;23(5):583-589. doi:10.1093/intqhc/mzr042. PMID: 21733978.

audits.title: [Lessons and impact of two audits on postpartum hemorrhages in 24 maternity hospitals of the network "Sécurité Naissance - Naître Ensemble" in "Pays-de-la-Loire" area].
audits.standard: CNGOF guidelines and HAS 2004 criteria for postpartum haemorrhage

cycle1.result: Time of PPH noted 66%; specific monitoring sheet 0%; blood loss noted 51%; sulprostone within 30 minutes 53%; decision within 2 hours 47%.

audits.intervention: Corrective actions: specific monitoring sheet, recording blood loss, transfusion on clinical criteria, earlier sulprostone, agreements with visceral surgery and avoiding maternal transfers.

cycle2.result: Management compliance 81%; time of PPH noted 85%; monitoring sheet 87%; blood loss noted 67%; sulprostone within 30 minutes 58%; decision within 2 hours 69%.

audits.other_findings: Prevention compliance 73% of 239 vaginal deliveries, with low notification of blood loss (36%) and collection bag use (35%).
audits.citation: Branger B, Gillard P, Monrigal C, Thelu S, Robidas E, Viot S, et al.. [Lessons and impact of two audits on postpartum hemorrhages in 24 maternity hospitals of the network "Sécurité Naissance - Naître Ensemble" in "Pays-de-la-Loire" area]. J Gynecol Obstet Biol Reprod (Paris). 2011;40(7):657-667. doi:10.1016/j.jgyn.2011.06.016. PMID: 21940114.

audits.title: Clinical audit of postpartum hemorrhage at district-level and referral-level hospitals in southern Thailand.
audits.standard: Evidence-based checklist for immediate postpartum haemorrhage management
audits.setting: Three referral and six district hospitals, southern Thailand

cycle1.result: District level: retained Foley catheter 44%, close haemodynamic monitoring 67%. Referral level: retained Foley catheter 76%, uterine massage documented 67%.

audits.other_findings: Adherence was more likely in cases with severe blood loss or transfusion; documentation of treatment was incomplete.
audits.citation: Talungchit P, Liabsuetrakul T. Clinical audit of postpartum hemorrhage at district-level and referral-level hospitals in southern Thailand. J Med Assoc Thai. 2012;95(10):1244-1251. PMID: 23193735.

audits.title: Severe postpartum haemorrhage after vaginal delivery: a statistical process control chart to report seven years of continuous quality improvement.
audits.standard: Criteria-based audit of recommended procedures for severe postpartum haemorrhage
audits.setting: Maternity unit, Rhone-Alpes region (Reseau perinatal Aurore, Lyon)

cycle1.result: Severe PPH prevalence 1.2% of vaginal deliveries.

audits.intervention: Quarterly clinical audit meetings analysing all severe PPH cases with feedback using statistical process control charts.

cycle2.result: Severe PPH prevalence 0.6% of vaginal deliveries (50% reduction).

audits.other_findings: Performance rate of each recommended procedure was also monitored; figures not given in the abstract.
audits.citation: Dupont C, Occelli P, Deneux-Tharaux C, Touzet S, Duclos A, Bouvier-Colle MH, et al.. Severe postpartum haemorrhage after vaginal delivery: a statistical process control chart to report seven years of continuous quality improvement. Eur J Obstet Gynecol Reprod Biol. 2014;178:169-175. doi:10.1016/j.ejogrb.2014.04.021. PMID: 24813084.

audits.title: Major obstetric haemorrhage of 2000 ml or greater: a clinical audit.
audits.setting: Oxford University Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust

cycle1.result: Poor compliance (<75%) with MOH call activation (52%), anaesthetic consultant presence (63%) and tranexamic acid (46%); 30/56 (54%) acutely transfused.

audits.intervention: Guideline revised and staff training including simulation held after the audit.
audits.other_findings: Non-acutely transfused women needed secondary transfusion more often without an MOH call (33% vs 10%, p = .052).
audits.citation: O'Sullivan J, Mansfield R, Talbot R, Cairns AE. Major obstetric haemorrhage of 2000 ml or greater: a clinical audit. J Obstet Gynaecol. 2018;38(8):1065-1072. doi:10.1080/01443615.2018.1449820. PMID: 29724141.

audits.title: Appropriate Documentation of the Timing of Events in the Management of Women with Postpartum Hemorrhage in Aminu Kano Teaching Hospital: A 2-Year Audit.
audits.standard: RCOG guidelines on documentation of timing of events in postpartum haemorrhage management
audits.setting: Department of Obstetrics and Gynaecology, Aminu Kano Teaching Hospital (teaching hospital labour ward)

cycle1.result: Standards achieved: initial assessment 85%, resuscitation 78.6%, investigations 85.7%; 61% treated within recommended time; 56% received appropriate uterotonics; appropriate documentation of major surgery 12%.

audits.other_findings: PPH incidence was 2.48% (129 of 5202 labour ward patients). Timing of major surgical interventions was the weakest area.
audits.citation: Garba Z, Abdullahi HM, Yusuf M, Takai IU, Muhammad ID. Appropriate Documentation of the Timing of Events in the Management of Women with Postpartum Hemorrhage in Aminu Kano Teaching Hospital: A 2-Year Audit. Niger Med J. 2019;60(1):9-12. doi:10.4103/nmj.nmj_5_19. PMID: 31413428.

audits.title: How to improve the quality of care for women with postpartum haemorrhage at Onandjokwe Hospital, Namibia: quality improvement study.
audits.standard: Criterion-based target standards for structure (19), process (9) and outcome (3) of PPH care

cycle1.result: 12/19 structural, 0/9 process and 0/3 outcome target standards achieved.

audits.intervention: Audit team planned and implemented interventions to improve quality of care over 10 months (details not given in abstract).

cycle2.result: 19/19 structural, 6/9 process and 2/3 outcome target standards met.

audits.other_findings: One maternal death at baseline and none at follow-up; 6/9 process and 2/3 outcome criteria improved significantly.
audits.citation: Nsangamay T, Mash R. How to improve the quality of care for women with postpartum haemorrhage at Onandjokwe Hospital, Namibia: quality improvement study. BMC Pregnancy Childbirth. 2019;19(1):489. doi:10.1186/s12884-019-2635-6. PMID: 31829139.

audits.title: Designing and implementing an all Wales postpartum haemorrhage quality improvement project: OBS Cymru (the Obstetric Bleeding Strategy for Wales).
audits.standard: Obstetric Bleeding Strategy for Wales and All Wales Guideline
audits.setting: All 12 obstetric units in Wales (OBS Cymru)

cycle1.result: Documented risk assessment 0%; objective blood loss measurement 52%; point-of-care coagulation testing for PPH >=1500 mL 38%

audits.intervention: Risk assessment, objective blood loss measurement, multiprofessional bedside assessment at 1000 mL, point-of-care coagulation testing, All Wales Guideline, PPH proforma and standardised training

cycle2.result: Risk assessment 76%; objective measurement 88%; point-of-care testing 59%

audits.other_findings: 94% of staff aware of the project; PPH >=2500 mL incidence 6.03 per 1000 maternities.
audits.citation: Bell SF, Kitchen T, John M, Scarr C, Kelly K, Bailey C, et al.. Designing and implementing an all Wales postpartum haemorrhage quality improvement project: OBS Cymru (the Obstetric Bleeding Strategy for Wales). audits.title: Quality of care in prevention, detection and management of postpartum hemorrhage in hospitals in Afghanistan: an observational assessment.
audits.standard: Quality of care standards for PPH prevention, detection and management
audits.setting: 87 public and private hospitals (district, provincial, regional, specialty)

cycle1.result: Uterotonics for PPH prevention in 73.3% (district), 71.2% (provincial/regional/specialty) and 72.7% (private); blood loss monitoring 48.4%, 36.9% and 43.3%; manual removal for retained placenta 97.8%.

audits.other_findings: Placenta completeness checked in about half of women; oxytocin available in about 90% of public hospitals but misoprostol in only 52.5-56.8%.
audits.citation: Ansari N, Maruf F, Manalai P, Currie S, Soroush MS, Amin SS, et al.. Quality of care in prevention, detection and management of postpartum hemorrhage in hospitals in Afghanistan: an observational assessment. BMC Health Serv Res. 2020;20(1):484. doi:10.1186/s12913-020-05342-y. PMID: 32487154.

audits.title: Introduction of Criterion-Based Audit of Postpartum Hemorrhage in a University Hospital in Eastern Ethiopia: Implementation and Considerations.
audits.standard: Eight standard criteria for PPH management adapted to the local setting
audits.setting: Hiwot Fana Specialized University Hospital, Harar

cycle1.result: All eight criteria met in 3 of 45 women (6.7%); low criteria: IV line set-up 71.1%, vital sign monitoring 51.1%, typing and cross-matching 48.9%, fluid chart 13.3%.

audits.other_findings: Deficiencies in documentation, monitoring, blood availability and delays were found; local recommendations and an intervention plan were drawn up.

audits.setting: All hospital deliveries in Suriname (national study)

cycle1.result: In severe PPH: prophylactic oxytocin 61.3% (95/155), oxytocin treatment 68.8% (106/154), tranexamic acid 4.9% (5/103).

audits.title: Using Criteria-Based Audit to Improve the Management of Postpartum Haemorrhage in a University Hospital in Eastern Ethiopia: A Before and After Study.
audits.standard: Eight co-created criteria-based audit criteria for postpartum haemorrhage management
audits.setting: Tertiary university hospital (Hiwot Fana Comprehensive Specialized Hospital, Harar)

cycle1.result: Only 6.7% (3/45) women met all audit criteria.

cycle2.result: 22% (12/55) met all criteria (p = 0.03); criteria met ranged from 24% (13/55) for fluid monitoring to 100% (55/55) for admission history and haemoglobin measurement.

audits.other_findings: Barriers: no management template, no refresher training, no emergency kit and inadequate blood for transfusion.
audits.citation: Girma S, van den Akker T, van Roosmalen J, Ahmed SS, Ahmed R, Mengistu S, et al.. Using Criteria-Based Audit to Improve the Management of Postpartum Haemorrhage in a University Hospital in Eastern Ethiopia: A Before and After Study. Trop Med Int Health. 2026;31(3):307-314. doi:10.1111/tmi.70069. PMID: 41454592.

audits.title: Lessons learned from nationwide perinatal audit of severe postpartum haemorrhage in the Netherlands.
audits.standard: National and local guidelines and standards for PPH management
audits.setting: Nationwide perinatal audit via regional perinatal cooperation groups

cycle1.result: 234 improvable care factors: nonadherence to guidelines and standards 47.8%, organisation of care 22.3%, communication and documentation 17.1%

audits.other_findings: Common issues were absent or ambiguous local protocols, unclear responsibilities, limited staffing and labour room capacity.
audits.citation: Broeders L, Koenen SV, de Vocht N, van den Akker T, Rosman AN. Lessons learned from nationwide perinatal audit of severe postpartum haemorrhage in the Netherlands. Int J Qual Health Care. 2026;38(3):mzag119. doi:10.1093/intqhc/mzag119. PMID: 42640571.

audits.title: A French audit of maternity unit protocols for immediate postpartum hemorrhage: A cross-sectional study (HERA).
audits.standard: 2004 French guidelines for prevention and management of postpartum haemorrhage (16 criteria)
audits.setting: Maternity units in volunteer French perinatal networks

cycle1.result: 97.1% had a written protocol but only 67.0% (159/237) a local protocol; blood loss quantification 83.5%; PPH defined in 25.3%; recording time of diagnosis 53.2% and blood loss volume 55.7%.

audits.other_findings: Results differed only slightly by maternity unit level or status.

audits.title: Leveraging a criteria-based audit approach to identify challenges and develop strategies to improve management of postpartum hemorrhage: A case study from the Dominican Republic.
audits.standard: Eight evidence-based criteria for postpartum haemorrhage management
audits.setting: La Maternidad Renee Klang Viuda Guzman Hospital, Santiago

cycle1.result: 25% compliance with evidence-based criteria; gaps in maternal risk assessment, provider training and protocol use.

audits.intervention: PPH toolkit, protocol and simulation-based training.
audits.other_findings: 12 of 13 toolkit users (92%) felt it improved timely management; 59 healthcare workers surveyed.
audits.citation: Voigt P, Ramos B, Hernandez S, Hernandez R, Jimenez M, Collado C, et al.. Leveraging a criteria-based audit approach to identify challenges and develop strategies to improve management of postpartum hemorrhage: A case study from the Dominican Republic.
